findings.description: PromotionOrchestrator.promote() did not enforce model/dependency compatibility. The CompatibilityChecker existed but was never wired into the promotion path, so a challenger trained on a DIFFERENT feature_version/label_version than the incumbent champion could be promoted purely on a higher IC — a non-like-for-like replacement that breaks provenance continuity.
findings.reproduction: Promote champion A (feature_version=feat-v3). Register + advance challenger B (feature_version=feat-v99) with higher IC. Call promote(scope, B, ev_B, ev_A, ...). Before fix: outcome=PROMOTE, champion becomes B. Reproduced by an independent probe and captured in tests/test_phase3p.py::TestLifecycleRedTeam::test_promotion_fail_closed (case d).
findings.impact: A model with an incompatible feature/label contract could silently become champion, invalidating downstream inference and evidence provenance.
findings.fix: promote() now computes feature_version + label_version compatibility (reusing the existing CompatibilityChecker) against the current champion and returns a BLOCKED decision on INCOMPATIBLE, before any state mutation. Compatible challengers still promote (verified — no false positive).

findings.description: _atomic_promote() flipped the champion pointer (step 3) BEFORE advancing the registry state (step 4). If the challenger was not PROMOTION_ELIGIBLE, _advance_to_champion raised AFTER the pointer was already flipped, leaving champion=x@v1 while the registry record stayed REGISTERED. recover_pending() then compared the flipped pointer to the intent target, mis-classified it as 'committed', cleared the intent, and permanently left a champion whose registry record was never advanced — a divergent, non-fail-closed state. Promotion was not truly atomic despite the module docstring claiming it was.
findings.reproduction: Register challenger x@v1 but do NOT advance it past REGISTERED. Call promote(...). Before fix: PromotionError raised, but champion pointer = x@v1 and registry state = REGISTERED; recover_pending() retained the divergent champion. Reproduced by independent probe; captured in tests/test_phase3p.py::TestLifecycleRedTeam::test_promotion_fail_closed (case b).
findings.impact: A crash or an ineligible challenger during promotion could leave the system with a champion pointer inconsistent with the registry, silently bypassing eligibility/soak requirements.
findings.fix: Registry eligibility is validated UP FRONT — in promote() (returns BLOCKED if state not in {PROMOTION_ELIGIBLE, CHAMPION}) and defensively at the top of _atomic_promote() (raises PromotionError before ANY write). An ineligible challenger now causes ZERO state change: no champion pointer, registry unchanged, no dangling recovery intent (verified).

findings.description: Initial suspicion (from a static behavioral map) that ModelIdentity.identity_hash excludes dataset_version/universe_version and could collide across materially different identities. Independent executable probe DISPROVED this: identity_hash differs when dataset_version/universe_version differ. No collision exists. Recorded for transparency — verifying from behavior corrected an inaccurate static claim (spec §5).
findings.reproduction: Build two ModelIdentity with identical model_id@version but different dataset_version + universe_version; identity_hash values differ.
